summary: Michael L. Walter (1948–2020) worked in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Larry William Moses, was a Research Fellow at the Lumbini International Research Institute (attested 2000), and served as Special Languages Cataloger at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2020).
Michael M. Broido worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge and held an appointment at the University of Oxford.

Michael Oppitz (born 1942) is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He held a post at the Institute for Advanced Study, Berlin (~1987–1988) and served as Leiter at the University of Zurich (~1991–2008).
Michael P. Berman works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Attested in 2012, he served as a professor at Brock University and as managing editor of the Canadian Journal of Buddhist Studies.

Michael Puett (born 1964) is a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1986–1994) under Marshall Sahlins and Anthony C. Yu, and has held professorships at Harvard University (~1994, ~2013).

Michael Pye (born 1939) works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Cambridge and Leeds under Maurice Frank Wiles, and held posts at Leeds (~1968–1978), Marburg (1982–2004), Lancaster (1991–1994), and Otani University (~2005–2007).

Michael R. Sheehy works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from CIIS (attested 2007) under Steven D. Goodman and Khenpo Kunga Sherab Salje, and held posts at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center and the University of Virginia (attested 2019–2026).

Michael Radich specializes in Buddhist studies, computational fields, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard (~2001–2007) and held posts at Victoria University of Wellington (2005–2017), Kyoto University (2009), University of Hamburg (2013–2014), and Heidelberg University (2018).
Michael S. Drummond specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at the University of Bristol and was a PhD candidate at Utrecht University (attested 2006).

Michael Schmidt worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts with the Katalogisierung der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland (1992), at the University of Göttingen (attested 1995), and as a dictionary editor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 1981).

Michael Silverstein (1945–2020) was a linguist who studied at Stuyvesant High School (~1959–1962) and Harvard University (~1962–1972). He spent his career on the faculty at the University of Chicago (~1970–2020).
Michael Soltys studied under Stephen Cook and Alasdair Urquhart from ~1995 to 2001.

Michael Stanley-Baker specializes in Sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He completed an MA at Indiana University Bloomington under Stephen R. Bokenkamp (attested 2006) and held posts at the Max Planck Institute, University of Leipzig, University of Pittsburgh, and Nanyang Technological University.
Michael Torsten Much (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied as a fellow at the University of Hamburg and studied under Ernst Steinkellner (attested 1991).

Michael Viggo Fausbøll (1821–1908) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (1838–1847) under Niels Ludvig Westergaard, later serving there as assistant librarian (1861) and Professor of Indian Philology (1878–1902).

Michael W. Meister (born 1942) works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Harvard University (BA 1960–1964, MA 1968–1971, PhD 1971–1974) and the University of Pennsylvania, where he became a professor in ~1976.

Michael Weiers (1937–2025) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He completed his dissertation at the University of Bonn (~1960–1965), where he was a professor (1972–2003), and held an honorary professorship at Inner Mongolia University (~1999).

Michael Willis specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Victoria and University of Chicago (PhD 1988) and held posts at SUNY New Paltz, the Royal Asiatic Society, and the British Museum (curator, 1994–2014).

Michael Witzel (born 1943) works in Indology and linguistics. He led the Nepal Research Centre (1972–1978), held the Sanskrit chair at Leiden University (1978–1986), and has served as professor and Chair of Sanskrit at Harvard University (1986, 2022).

Michael Zimmermann (born 1966) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and others, later holding posts at Stanford University (2003) and the University of Hamburg (attested 2009–2026).
